name: Wealth Advisory — Institutional Context
desc: The kind of knowledge that shapes every advice decision but never shows up in the CRM. Strategy, judgment, unwritten rules, institutional memory, language, work-unit intelligence, relationships, and exceptions.

nodes.label: Why we say no to certain clients
nodes.desc: The real client-acceptance criteria that never made it into the formal policy. When the gut says this one will be trouble and why. Not in any document.

nodes.label: The 60-second gut check on a new client
nodes.desc: What senior advisers actually look at and feel in the first meeting. The signals that say good fit or walk away before any formal process runs.

nodes.label: What we never put in an email
nodes.desc: Sensitive client or compliance topics that are discussed in person or on the phone only. The real information boundary that is not in the policy.

nodes.label: The last time we saw this situation
nodes.desc: Anonymised we had a client like this — what we did, what we would do differently. Exists in senior heads and hallway conversations only.

nodes.label: Words we never use with HNW clients
nodes.desc: The phrasing that signals we get it vs we are reading from a script. The vocabulary that distinguishes the firm's best communicators.

nodes.label: What we actually check before a review meeting
nodes.desc: The order an experienced adviser reads the file, what they flag, what they ignore. The real prep sequence that is not in the process map.

nodes.label: Who to ask before going to compliance
nodes.desc: The informal path for is this okay that avoids a formal ticket. Who has the judgment and the authority to give a quick read.

nodes.label: When we made an exception and why
nodes.desc: Concrete examples where the rule was bent — client type, situation, and the reasoning that made it acceptable. The real ontology.
